name: Amalek
charge: Smiting the hindmost, the feeble and faint and weary, when Israel came out of Egypt; and he feared not God
summary: Amalek, the grandson of Esau, was the first nation to come against Israel after Egypt. He did not meet the mighty men in front; he crept up behind and smote the hindmost, the feeble, the faint and the weary, and he did not fear God. The Lord swore war with Amalek from generation to generation and had it written for a memorial: Saul spared Agag, Samuel hewed him in pieces, Haman the Agagite rose in Persia, and the war runs on to the end of the world, when Jacob bruises the head.
offenseFull: Then came Amalek and fought with Israel in Rephidim (Exodus 17:8). This was no stranger’s war. Timna was concubine to Eliphaz, Esau’s son, and bore him Amalek, and Amalek is named a duke among the dukes that came of Eliphaz in the land of Edom (Genesis 36:12, 16). That is the elite of Esau’s line, and the battle between the two brothers carried into the next generation.

The manner of the attack is the charge, and Moses rehearsed it forty years later so it could not be forgotten: remember what Amalek did to Israel by the way when they came forth out of Egypt, how he met them by the way and smote the hindmost of them, even all that were feeble behind, when they were faint and weary, and he feared not God (Deuteronomy 25:17-18). In a caravan the strong men walk in front; in the back are the old, the women, the babies and the lame. Rather than meet the mighty men head on, Amalek came up from behind, killed the feeble, and waited until Israel was tired and worn out to do it. They knew exactly who Israel was; those were their cousins. That same spirit works against the young and the old of this nation to this day.
judgmentFull: When Moses held up his hand Israel prevailed, and when he let down his hand Amalek prevailed; so they put a stone under him, and Aaron and Hur stayed up his hands, the one on the one side and the other on the other side, until the going down of the sun, and Joshua discomfited Amalek with the edge of the sword (Exodus 17:11-13). Moses was about eighty years old holding a rod above his head all day; the fathers were mighty men. The sign showed the people whose hand their life was in. Then the Lord told Moses to write it for a memorial in a book and rehearse it in the ears of Joshua, because he would utterly put out the remembrance of Amalek from under heaven, and had sworn to have war with Amalek from generation to generation (Exodus 17:14-16). Balaam pronounced the end of it: Amalek was the first of the nations, meaning the first nation to make war on Israel coming out of Egypt, but his latter end shall be that he perish for ever (Numbers 24:20).

Hundreds of years later the Lord still remembered what Amalek did to Israel and how he laid wait for him in the way, and sent Saul by Samuel to smite Amalek and utterly destroy all that they had (1 Samuel 15:2-3). Christianity says forgive and forget, but the Most High said remember; the law against bearing a grudge is toward the children of a man’s own people (Leviticus 19:18). Israel were no tyrants in it either: the Kenites were warned to depart from among the Amalekites before the sword came, for the kindness they had showed Israel coming up out of Egypt (1 Samuel 15:6). Saul spared Agag, and Samuel hewed Agag in pieces before the Lord in Gilgal (1 Samuel 15:33); of that seed Haman the Agagite rose in Persia to destroy the whole nation, and was hanged on his own gallows (Esther 3:1; Esther 7:10). The war runs from generation to generation. Today that seed says they are Jews and are not, but are the synagogue of Satan, and the Lord will make them come and worship before Israel’s feet and know that he has loved us (Revelation 2:9; Revelation 3:9). The enmity was set in the garden between the serpent’s seed and the woman’s seed; they bruised Christ’s heel, and at the end of the world the God of peace will bruise Satan under the feet of his people (Genesis 3:15; Romans 16:20; 2 Esdras 6:7-10). The command to blot out Amalek belongs to the kingdom and to the Lord’s timing, written in his book; it is not a licence for any man’s hand now, for Israel is to live peaceably with all men (Deuteronomy 25:19; Romans 12:18).

lawsResolved.text: When forces march out to battle, a detachment is to remain to watch over the camp.
War as a defense from unprovoked attack.
We are not to have pity or mercy on heathen or ungodly enemies, but are to destroy all those who God shall deliver to us.

text.text: Then came Amalek, and fought with Israel in Rephidim.
And Timna was concubine to Eliphaz Esau’s son; and she bare to Eliphaz Amalek: these were the sons of Adah Esau’s wife.
Duke Korah, duke Gatam, and duke Amalek: these are the dukes that came of Eliphaz in the land of Edom; these were the sons of Adah.
Remember what Amalek did unto thee by the way, when ye were come forth out of Egypt;
How he met thee by the way, and smote the hindmost of thee, even all that were feeble behind thee, when thou wast faint and weary; and he feared not God.
And it came to pass, when Moses held up his hand, that Israel prevailed: and when he let down his hand, Amalek prevailed.

But Moses’ hands were heavy; and they took a stone, and put it under him, and he sat thereon; and Aaron and Hur stayed up his hands, the one on the one side, and the other on the other side; and his hands were steady until the going down of the sun.
And Joshua discomfited Amalek and his people with the edge of the sword.
And the Lord said unto Moses, Write this for a memorial in a book, and rehearse it in the ears of Joshua: for I will utterly put out the remembrance of Amalek from under heaven.
And Moses built an altar, and called the name of it JEHOVAH–nissi:
For he said, Because the Lord hath sworn that the Lord will have war with Amalek from generation to generation.
And when he looked on Amalek, he took up his parable, and said, Amalek was the first of the nations; but his latter end shall be that he perish for ever.
Thus saith the Lord of hosts, I remember that which Amalek did to Israel, how he laid wait for him in the way, when he came up from Egypt.
Now go and smite Amalek, and utterly destroy all that they have, and spare them not; but slay both man and woman, infant and suckling, ox and sheep, camel and ass.
Thou shalt not avenge, nor bear any grudge against the children of thy people, but thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself: I am the Lord.

And Saul said unto the Kenites, Go, depart, get you down from among the Amalekites, lest I destroy you with them: for ye shewed kindness to all the children of Israel, when they came up out of Egypt. So the Kenites departed from among the Amalekites.
And Samuel said, As thy sword hath made women childless, so shall thy mother be childless among women. And Samuel hewed Agag in pieces before the Lord in Gilgal.
After these things did king Ahasuerus promote Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, and advanced him, and set his seat above all the princes that were with him.
So they hanged Haman on the gallows that he had prepared for Mordecai. Then was the king’s wrath pacified.
I know thy works, and tribulation, and poverty, (but thou art rich) and I know the blasphemy of them which say they are Jews, and are not, but are the synagogue of Satan.
Behold, I will make them of the synagogue of Satan, which say they are Jews, and are not, but do lie; behold, I will make them to come and worship before thy feet, and to know that I have loved thee.
And I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel.
And the God of peace shall bruise Satan under your feet shortly. The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you. Amen.
Then answered I and said, What shall be the parting asunder of the times? or when shall be the end of the first, and the beginning of it that followeth?
And he said unto me, From Abraham unto Isaac, when Jacob and Esau were born of him, Jacob’s hand held first the heel of Esau.
For Esau is the end of the world, and Jacob is the beginning of it that followeth.
The hand of man is betwixt the heel and the hand: other question, Esdras, ask thou not.

Therefore it shall be, when the Lord thy God hath given thee rest from all thine enemies round about, in the land which the Lord thy God giveth thee for an inheritance to possess it, that thou shalt blot out the remembrance of Amalek from under heaven; thou shalt not forget it.
If it be possible, as much as lieth in you, live peaceably with all men.
Then came Amalek, and fought with Israel in Rephidim.
And Moses said unto Joshua, Choose us out men, and go out, fight with Amalek: to morrow I will stand on the top of the hill with the rod of God in mine hand.
So Joshua did as Moses had said to him, and fought with Amalek: and Moses, Aaron, and Hur went up to the top of the hill.
And it came to pass, when Moses held up his hand, that Israel prevailed: and when he let down his hand, Amalek prevailed.

But Moses’ hands were heavy; and they took a stone, and put it under him, and he sat thereon; and Aaron and Hur stayed up his hands, the one on the one side, and the other on the other side; and his hands were steady until the going down of the sun.
And Joshua discomfited Amalek and his people with the edge of the sword.
And the Lord said unto Moses, Write this for a memorial in a book, and rehearse it in the ears of Joshua: for I will utterly put out the remembrance of Amalek from under heaven.
And Moses built an altar, and called the name of it JEHOVAH–nissi:
For he said, Because the Lord hath sworn that the Lord will have war with Amalek from generation to generation.
Remember what Amalek did unto thee by the way, when ye were come forth out of Egypt;
How he met thee by the way, and smote the hindmost of thee, even all that were feeble behind thee, when thou wast faint and weary; and he feared not God.

Therefore it shall be, when the Lord thy God hath given thee rest from all thine enemies round about, in the land which the Lord thy God giveth thee for an inheritance to possess it, that thou shalt blot out the remembrance of Amalek from under heaven; thou shalt not forget it.
